literal: Through the sevenfold seven births also, they will remember, in their distress, the friendship of those who wiped it away.
translation: Through all the sevenfold births of existence, people will cherish the friendship of those who wiped away their distress.
modern: தங்களுடைய துன்பத்தைத் துடைத்தவருடைய நட்பினை, மக்கள் ஏழு வகையான பிறவிகளிலும் நினைத்துப் போற்றுவர்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the enduring nature of gratitude. The phrase 'ezhumai ezhu pirappum' refers to the classical concept of the sevenfold cycle of births, representing eternity or all future lifetimes. The poet states that when someone wipes away ('tudaittavar') another's deep distress ('vizhumam'), that act of friendship ('natpu') is so profound that the recipient will remember and cherish it ('ulluvar') throughout all their future births. It emphasizes that true help received during a crisis creates an immortal bond of gratitude.
